findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued is a single import-time timestamp and does not survive the task hop
findings.body: queued is declared as queued: datetime = timezone.now() on a dataclass. That call runs once, when the class body is executed, not when each AssignmentSource is constructed, and it is not a field(default_factory=...). Every source built via from_integration() therefore shares one timestamp from process import, so distinct rapid assignee events cannot be ordered or deduped by queued. to_dict() then puts that raw datetime into the Celery kwargs of sync_assignee_outbound. A JSON task serializer turns it into an ISO string; from_dict() does cls(**input_dict) with no parsing and no runtime type check, and only traps ValueError/TypeError, so reconstruction succeeds with queued as a str. Nothing in the new tests round-trips to_dict() through from_dict(), so this ships uncaught. Cycle suppression still works today because only integration_id is read, but the timestamp this carrier was added to record is wrong both before and after the queue.

findings.title: Same-integration guard skips every linked issue, not just the one that webhooked
findings.body: should_sync returns False whenever sync_source.integration_id matches the installation's integration, before looking at which external issue is being updated. sync_group_assignee_outbound enqueues one task per GroupLink and each task applies that same check. A group linked to two issues on one Jira (or other) integration will therefore not push the new assignee to the sibling ticket after an inbound change. Previously every linked external issue was updated. AssignmentSource only stores source_name, integration_id, and queued, so the worker cannot skip write-back only for the issue key that fired the webhook. Sibling tickets keep a stale assignee until someone assigns the Sentry issue directly. A write to a different issue on that integration would not by itself loop if the mapped Sentry user is unchanged, because GroupAssignee.assign does not emit outbound sync when the user id does not change.

findings.title: Tests never prove other integrations still sync, or that inbound wiring suppresses the echo
findings.body: The new test only assigns with AssignmentSource.from_integration on the same single integration and asserts sync_assignee_outbound was not called. A regression that skips outbound sync whenever any assignment_source is set would still pass, and so would removing assignment_source= from sync_group_assignee_inbound. Nothing covers a second linked integration still receiving the outbound call, deassign with a matching source, or from_dict(to_dict()) preserving integration_id and a real datetime. Those are the behaviors this change claims to preserve or rely on.
